intro.quote: Consider a VM within a VXLAN overlay network.  This VM is unaware of VXLAN.  To communicate with a VM on a different host, it sends a MAC frame destined to the target as normal.

steps.explain: After delivering the frame, the remote VTEP learns the inner source MAC to outer source IP mapping, so the destination VM's response packet does not need unknown-destination flooding.

cite.quote: In addition to forwarding the packet to the destination VM, the remote VTEP learns the mapping from inner source MAC to outer source IP address.  It stores this mapping in a table so that when the destination VM sends a response packet, there is no need for an "unknown destination" flooding of the response packet.

sequences.title: ARP Exchange over a Multicast VXLAN Segment

intro.quote: Consider the VM on the source host attempting to communicate with the destination VM using IP.  Assuming that they are both on the same subnet, the VM sends out an Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) broadcast frame.

steps.explain: The destination VM sends a standard ARP response over IP unicast. It is encapsulated back to the VTEP connected to the originating VM because the tunnel endpoint mapping was learned through the earlier ARP request.

cite.quote: The destination VM sends a standard ARP response using IP unicast.  This frame will be encapsulated back to the VTEP connecting the originating VM using IP unicast VXLAN encapsulation.  This is possible since the mapping of the ARP response's destination MAC to the VXLAN tunnel end point IP was learned earlier through the ARP request.

intro.quote: VXLAN Header:  This is an 8-byte field that has:

fields.name: Flags
fields.explain: The I flag is set for a valid VNI. The other seven bits are reserved, sent as zero, and ignored on receipt.

cite.quote: Flags (8 bits): where the I flag MUST be set to 1 for a valid VXLAN Network ID (VNI).  The other 7 bits (designated "R") are reserved fields and MUST be set to zero on transmission and ignored on receipt.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.explain: This 24-bit reserved area is sent as zero and ignored on receipt.

cite.quote: Reserved fields (24 bits and 8 bits): MUST be set to zero on transmission and ignored on receipt.

fields.name: VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI)
fields.explain: The VNI designates the individual overlay network on which the communicating VMs are situated, and VMs on different overlay networks cannot communicate with each other.

cite.quote: VXLAN Segment ID/VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI): this is a 24-bit value used to designate the individual VXLAN overlay network on which the communicating VMs are situated.  VMs in different VXLAN overlay networks cannot communicate with each other.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.explain: This 8-bit reserved area is sent as zero and ignored on receipt.

cite.quote: Reserved fields (24 bits and 8 bits): MUST be set to zero on transmission and ignored on receipt.

intro.quote: Outer UDP Header:  This is the outer UDP header with a source port provided by the VTEP and the destination port being a well-known UDP port.

fields.name: Source Port
fields.explain: The RFC recommends deriving the source port from a hash of inner-packet fields to provide entropy for ECMP load balancing.

cite.quote: Source Port:  It is recommended that the UDP source port number be calculated using a hash of fields from the inner packet -- one example being a hash of the inner Ethernet frame's headers.  This is to enable a level of entropy for the ECMP/load-balancing of the VM-to-VM traffic across the VXLAN overlay.

fields.name: Destination Port
fields.explain: The default destination port is 4789, and the port should be configurable for interoperability with early implementations.

cite.quote: Destination Port: IANA has assigned the value 4789 for the VXLAN UDP port, and this value SHOULD be used by default as the destination UDP port.  Some early implementations of VXLAN have used other values for the destination port.  To enable interoperability with these implementations, the destination port SHOULD be configurable.

fields.name: UDP Length
fields.explain: Carries the length of the UDP datagram.

fields.name: UDP Checksum
fields.explain: A zero checksum should be sent, and a received zero checksum must be accepted for decapsulation.

cite.quote: UDP Checksum: It SHOULD be transmitted as zero.  When a packet is received with a UDP checksum of zero, it MUST be accepted for decapsulation.
